wholeQuestion.question: Why can BMI underestimate nutrition risk?
choices: It does not distinguish muscle, fat, and fluid compartments
It is identical to percent weight loss
wholeQuestion.rationale: People with the same BMI can have very different body composition and trajectories.

choiceReview.choice: It does not distinguish muscle, fat, and fluid compartments
choiceReview.assessment: BMI describes mass relative to height, not separate muscle, fat or retained fluid; GLIM treats muscle mass separately and warns of fluid-confounded BMI.
Height is not always overestimated; this is not an inherent BMI property.
BMI is not a measurement of inflammation, which belongs to a separate etiologic domain.

choiceReview.choice: It is identical to percent weight loss
choiceReview.assessment: BMI uses weight and height, whereas percentage loss uses change relative to baseline.

wholeQuestion.question: A patient with obesity has clear temporal muscle loss and prolonged poor intake. What is the correct inference?
choices: A high BMI does not exclude malnutrition
Only underweight patients can be malnourished
wholeQuestion.rationale: Malnutrition can occur across the BMI spectrum.

choiceReview.choice: A high BMI does not exclude malnutrition
choiceReview.assessment: GLIM explicitly recognizes malnutrition in people with overweight or obesity; this inference does not by itself assign diagnostic severity.
High BMI does not establish adequate muscle mass.

choiceReview.choice: Only underweight patients can be malnourished
choiceReview.assessment: Malnutrition is not restricted to people with low BMI.
Reduced intake is relevant to the etiologic assessment.

wholeQuestion.question: Which GLIM phenotypic criterion can be present despite a normal BMI?
wholeQuestion.rationale: Muscle depletion can occur even when BMI is not low.

choiceReview.assessment: Low muscle mass is a separate phenotypic criterion and can occur without low BMI.
Disease burden is in the etiologic domain, not a phenotypic criterion.
Reduced assimilation is etiologic, not phenotypic.
Inflammation is etiologic, not phenotypic.

wholeQuestion.question: Which finding most directly confounds a rapid increase in body weight?
wholeQuestion.rationale: Fluid gain can increase scale weight without increasing tissue mass.

choiceReview.assessment: Fluid accumulation can increase measured weight and confound tissue interpretation.
Reduced appetite alone does not directly explain a rapid increase in measured weight.
Fat loss reduces a tissue compartment rather than directly explaining an increased scale weight.
Reduced grip describes function and does not directly account for a rapid scale-weight increase.

wholeQuestion.question: What does a single body weight fail to reveal?
choices: Direction, speed, and cause of change
The numerical mass at that moment
The unit used by the scale
Whether the scale displayed a value
wholeQuestion.rationale: Trajectory requires a credible baseline, time interval, and clinical context.

choiceReview.choice: Direction, speed, and cause of change
choiceReview.assessment: A single value does not supply a baseline, interval or causal history; GLIM and clinical assessment require trajectory and context.

choiceReview.choice: The numerical mass at that moment
choiceReview.assessment: The scale value supplies numerical mass, subject to measurement limitations.

choiceReview.choice: The unit used by the scale
choiceReview.assessment: A recorded weight can carry its unit; lacking trajectory is the relevant limitation among these options.

choiceReview.choice: Whether the scale displayed a value
choiceReview.assessment: Whether the scale displayed a value is an observation, not a trajectory or cause.

sources.scope: Phenotypic versus etiologic definitions; BMI limitations, obesity, muscle mass and fluid confounding. No new cutoff or numerical muscle threshold qualified in this phase.

Adult tool workflow, population and measurement limitations and alternative measures. Reading the charts does not independently validate each numeric chart cell. MUAC gives a general BMI category and must not be substituted into the BMI formula or assigned an actual MUST score. Special fluid/amputation interpretation requires the explanatory booklet; those question qualifications remain pending.
